children: was downgraded at HSBC on Friday as the investment firm said the hype from Meta Platforms
Muse artificial intelligence agent is adding volume but not conviction.

“We think the market is increasingly pricing Twilio as the communications infrastructure for Meta’s fast-growing Muse agent and the broader consumer agent ecosystem,” analyst Sameer Lam wrote in a note to clients. “We agree with the underlying industry logic that AI agents will expand communications volumes such as calls, messages, and authentications. Furthermore, we think Meta’s own AI voice stack limits Twilio’s ability to capture the highest value share of each Muse interaction. And we believe the market overestimates how much of that incremental value accrues to Twilio.”

Lam continued: “We see Twilio’s most likely Muse exposure as PSTN connectivity, which helps reaching a real phone number, followed by transactional and authentication messaging. Notably, these infrastructure layers are competitive and commoditized; Bandwidth, Sinch and others offer similar or more integrated PSTN connectivity. And we believe Meta could use Twilio, another CPaaS provider, or even connect more directly to wholesale carriers through SIP. Overall, we view the rising AI-agent traffic will benefit the industry, but it does not guarantee Twilio captures disproportionate economics.”
As such, Lam lowered his rating on Twilio to Reduce from Hold but kept his $211 price target on the stock.

title: Twilio downgraded at HSBC despite Muse-induced hype
